route.title: Train a tiny model on Shakespeare and read what it writes
route.whyChosen: These are the README's own CPU quick-start commands (install, prepare, small CPU train, sample), unchanged and with no uv prefix to drop. nanoGPT ships no pyproject.toml or setup.py, so there is nothing to `pip install -e`, and the README's install line is used as is.

install.cmd: pip install torch numpy tiktoken requests
install.trimmedFrom: pip install torch numpy transformers datasets tiktoken wandb tqdm

Overriding config with config/train_shakespeare_char.py:
# train a miniature character-level shakespeare model
# good for debugging and playing on macbooks and such

out_dir = 'out-shakespeare-char'
eval_interval = 250 # keep frequent because we'll overfit
eval_iters = 200
log_interval = 10 # don't print too too often

# we expect to overfit on this small dataset, so only save when val improves
always_save_checkpoint = False

wandb_log = False # override via command line if you like
wandb_project = 'shakespeare-char'
wandb_run_name = 'mini-gpt'

dataset = 'shakespeare_char'
gradient_accumulation_steps = 1
batch_size = 64
block_size = 256 # context of up to 256 previous characters

# baby GPT model :)
n_layer = 6
n_head = 6
n_embd = 384
dropout = 0.2

learning_rate = 1e-3 # with baby networks can afford to go a bit higher
max_iters = 5000
lr_decay_iters = 5000 # make equal to max_iters usually
min_lr = 1e-4 # learning_rate / 10 usually
beta2 = 0.99 # make a bit bigger because number of tokens per iter is small

warmup_iters = 100 # not super necessary potentially

# on macbook also add
# device = 'cpu'  # run on cpu only
# compile = False # do not torch compile the model

steps.title: See the map: prepare.py builds the data, train.py trains and writes a checkpoint, sample.py reads it and writes text (the README chains them in that order)
Train a tiny GPT on CPU

install: pip install torch numpy tiktoken requests
trapsToWarn: --temperature must be a float: pass 0.5 or 1.0, not 1, or the configurator's type assertion fails.
--init_from cannot contain a second =: the configurator splits each argument on = and fails with 'too many values to unpack'.
--start cannot contain =: the same split makes a value like A=B crash sample.py.
Flag names must match a config key exactly: a typo such as --temprature stops with 'Unknown config key'.
